description: A boundary that limits what a tool call can do, independently of what the policy or the model decided.
A file tool check that resolves every path against a root and refuses anything that is not the root or inside `root/`.
Escaping a folder with `..` segments or absolute paths, such as `notes/../../etc/passwd`.
The list of hosts (and schemes) an agent's network requests may reach; everything else is refused.
Server-side request forgery: making a server-side tool request internal addresses such as `localhost` or the cloud metadata endpoint `169.254.169.254`.
A URL whose host is an address instead of a name. Parsers normalize spellings like `0x7f000001` and `2130706433` to `127.0.0.1`.
An allowed hostname that resolves to a private address. Only checks on the resolved IP, usually in an egress proxy, catch it.
An allowed URL that redirects anywhere. Fetch tools must check every redirect target.
